settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: checkResource/isResourceUnderLocation and isInvalidEncodedPath in PathResourceResolver show the project does implement traversal guards elsewhere; comparable guards here are not present for the SpEL string.
Both parsing (lines 153-157) and evaluation (lines 220-227) are wrapped in broad catch(Throwable)/catch(SpelEvaluationException) blocks that only log, limiting error-based leakage or crash impact.
The class only sets selectorHeaderInUse = true after a successful parse, and evaluation failure simply excludes that subscription from matches.
No source line shows the selector value being used as a file path, command, or SQL input; only as a filter predicate evaluated to boolean.
candidates.description: DefaultSubscriptionRegistry allows a subscription message to carry a native header named by getSelectorHeaderName() (default "selector"). In addSubscriptionInternal (line 144) that header value is read and, if non-null, passed directly to this.expressionParser.parseExpression(selector) (line 147) with a plain SpelExpressionParser and no allowlist/sanitization of the expression string. The resulting Expression is stored on the subscription (line 159). Later, filterSubscriptions (lines 188-231) evaluates each stored selector expression with a StandardEvaluationContext built over the incoming message plus a SimpMessageHeaderPropertyAccessor (lines 211-214) and calls expression.getValue(context, boolean.class) (line 216). StandardEvaluationContext is the permissive SpEL evaluation context (it supports type references, constructors and, depending on configured resolvers, method invocation), in contrast to SimpleEvaluationContext, which is the restricted variant intended for untrusted expression input. The root cause is the combination of (a) an untrusted, client-supplied expression string and (b) evaluation under a permissive context. Preconditions/limits visible in source: the selector is taken from a native header of the SUBSCRIBE message, so whether the value is truly attacker-controlled depends on the surrounding STOMP/WebSocket channel and its inbound validation; parsing and evaluation are wrapped in broad try/catch(Throwable) handlers (lines 153-157 and 220-227) that log and continue, which suppresses exceptions but does not itself neutralize an expression that evaluates successfully; and no method/type restrictions are applied to the context. I could not confirm reachability of the client header to this method, nor any concrete impact (data access, side effects), so this is reported as an unconfirmed candidate rather than a demonstrated vulnerability.
missing_evidence: No trace in the reviewed source connecting a client-controlled STOMP frame header to addSubscriptionInternal with or without validation (the inbound channel/filter chain was not inspected).
No test in the reviewed test file exercises a malicious selector expression to show achievable impact.
No evidence of which type/method resolvers the StandardEvaluationContext exposes by default in this version, i.e. whether arbitrary type/method access is actually usable in evaluation.
Configuration-level controls (e.g., broker destination restrictions or header allowlists) that might prevent the selector header from reaching this code were not examined.
preconditions: A subscription (SUBSCRIBE frame) carrying the configured selector native header reaches DefaultSubscriptionRegistry.addSubscriptionInternal.
The selector header value is controlled by an untrusted party (client) without upstream validation/allowlisting.
The application uses the default or a configurably permissive selector header name and does not disable selector usage.
A subsequent message is matched to the subscription so that filterSubscriptions evaluates the stored expression.
candidates.title: Subscription selector header parsed as a raw SpEL expression and evaluated with a StandardEvaluationContext in DefaultSubscriptionRegistry
